# Incident Report: NetSupport RAT Infection — 2024-11-26

## Evidence reviewed
- `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (26,922 frames, ~20.8 MB) analyzed with tshark
- `2024-11-26-traffic-analysis-exercise-alerts.txt` / `.png` (exported Suricata/IDS alert log, RealTime Events view)

## 1. Infected host

| Attribute | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.11.26.183** | Consistent source IP across all malicious traffic |
| MAC address | **d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b** | ARP (`who-has`/`is-at` for 10.11.26.183) and Ethernet source address |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** | NBNS name registration (`<00>` Workstation, `<20>` Server service) from 10.11.26.183 |
| AD domain | nemotoads.health (NetBIOS: NEMOTODES; DC hostname NEMOTODE-DC at 10.11.26.3) | NBNS, DNS SRV lookups (`_ldap._tcp...nemotoads.health`), Kerberos realm field |
| Logged-in Windows user | **oboomwald** | Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ exchanges between 10.11.26.183 and the DC (10.11.26.3), realm NEMOTODES.HEALTH |

The host is a domain-joined Windows workstation (SMB/DCE-RPC, LDAP, Kerberos, EFSRPC traffic to the DC at 10.11.26.3 is routine AD activity and not attributable to the malware).

## 2. Malware family

**NetSupport RAT** (malicious repurposing of the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-control client), delivered via a browser-based fake-update/cracked-software redirect chain.

**Attribution: signature-confirmed**, corroborated by behavioral evidence:
- ETPRO signature hits: `TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity` (65 matches) and `TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin` (2 matches) against 10.11.26.183 → 194.180.191.64:443
- ET signature hits: `NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin` / `NetSupport Remote Admin Response`, `NetSupport GeoLocation Lookup Request`
- Behavioral corroboration observed directly in the capture: HTTP `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3` on every outbound POST; POST body framed as `CMD=ENCD\nES=1\nDATA=<hex-encoded blob>` (the known NetSupport client‑to‑server check-in format); a GeoIP lookup to NetSupport's own infrastructure (`geo.netsupportsoftware.com`) immediately after infection; and a persistent ~60-second beacon interval to a single C2 host disguised as HTTPS (plaintext HTTP is spoken on TCP/443, not real TLS — confirmed by Wireshark protocol dissection showing `HTTP`, not `TLS`, on that stream).

## 3. Indicators of compromise (all observed directly in the pcap)

### Delivery chain (pre-infection browsing, all initiated by 10.11.26.183)
| Time (UTC) | Domain | Resolved IP | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 04:50:11 | classicgrand.com | 213.246.109.5 | TLS 1.3 session (encrypted, content not recoverable) |
| 04:50:14 | modandcrackedapk.com | 193.42.38.139 | Flagged by ET: `ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup` and `ZPHP Domain in TLS SNI` — known malicious ad/redirect domain class |
| 04:50:14–15:59 | confirmsubscription.com | 13.56.30.207, 52.8.34.0 | TLS session; part of the same redirect chain (fake-download/notification-spam pattern) |

These three domains form the observed infection vector: the workstation browsed a "cracked software"-themed redirect chain shortly before NetSupport RAT activity began. Because all three sessions used properly negotiated TLS, no file name or hash could be recovered from their payloads — only the domains/IPs are confirmed IOCs.

### Command-and-control
| Indicator | Value |
|---|---|
| C2 endpoint | **194.180.191.64:443** (plaintext HTTP over the HTTPS port, not real TLS) |
| C2 URL | `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` (POST) |
| Beacon pattern | POST every ~60 seconds, `User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3`, body `CMD=ENCD\nES=1\nDATA=<hex>` |
| Duration observed | 2024-11-26 04:50:45 UTC through at least 05:43:29 UTC (continuous, ~53 minutes, 65+ check-ins) |
| Supporting infra | `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` → **104.26.1.231** (TCP/80, `GET /location/loca.asp`) — legitimate NetSupport geolocation service queried by the RAT client at install time |

### Files / hashes
No executable, installer, or archive transfer was observable in cleartext anywhere in the capture (the only plaintext HTTP objects retrieved are benign: Microsoft NCSI connect-test text, an OCSP response, a Windows CTL `.cab` file, and an Adobe ARM version-check text file — none are payload delivery). The RAT's installer/dropper itself was delivered over properly encrypted TLS sessions to classicgrand.com/confirmsubscription.com, so **no file name or SHA256 hash can be grounded in this traffic**. Do not report a hash for this incident — none is derivable from the pcap.

## Summary
10.11.26.183 (DESKTOP-B8TQK49, user oboomwald, domain nemotoads.health) was infected with NetSupport RAT after browsing a cracked-software/ad-redirect chain (classicgrand.com → modandcrackedapk.com → confirmsubscription.com) around 04:50 UTC on 2024-11-26. Immediately after, the host performed a NetSupport GeoIP check-in and began sustained C2 beaconing to 194.180.191.64:443 using the NetSupport client protocol, continuing for the remainder of the capture. Attribution to NetSupport RAT is signature-confirmed (ETPRO/ET rules) and behaviorally corroborated by the observed User-Agent, POST format, and beacon cadence. No dropped file name or hash is recoverable from this capture because the delivery sessions were TLS-encrypted.
